name: Work & Business
description: Office, meetings and business vocabulary for the workplace (English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese).

entries.notes: A business relationship: person/company you provide professional services to.
One-page summary of work history and skills for job applications.
A person you work with; same as colleague but emphasizes shared workplace.
Collective: all employees of an organization, not one person.
List of topics to discuss at a meeting. Not a personal planner.
The written record of a meeting, not units of time.
A pause in work or activity; not a fracture or to break something.
A document folder/record, not a metal tool for smoothing surfaces.
A container for documents; not folding paper or cloth.
Arriving or completing at the expected hour; punctual.
Occupied with work or activity; not having free time.
Free or able to be reached; having time or resources.
Comments or information about performance; not emotional response.
Out of work; not working due to lack of employment.
The computer device, not the animal.
A display for showing information; not a mesh filter.
To apply for a job or position.
A person or document confirming your work experience; not a mention.
An academic credential from study; not temperature or angle.
A period of work, e.g. the night shift.
To receive money for work; not to deserve or merit.
Regular payments after retirement; not a lodging house.
To oversee or run operations; not to barely handle or cope.
Being answerable for results and actions; requiring explanation.
A formal job performance review; not an estimate of property value.
An evaluation of performance or skill; not a tax or fee.
Accumulated work not yet completed, not a list of past events.
A local office or location, not a tree part or division of a subject.
A short summary or overview, not detailed instructions.
Physical/mental exhaustion from work stress, not a failed project.
Potential to do something; ability to develop skills. Not current performance level.
Maximum amount that can be held or handled, or someone's ability in a role.
A promise or obligation to do something, not necessarily agreement or consensus.
Proven ability and knowledge to do a task well; a skill area.
Contest or rivalry with others; distinct from competence (ability).
External expert hired to advise, not permanent staff.
Written letters or emails exchanged; the actual documents, not the act.
Evaluation pointing out faults; can be constructive, not necessarily negative.
The act of handing over goods or completing a task; not the goods themselves.
A firm request or requirement; can mean supply-and-demand in economics.
Reduction to a lower rank or position, not dismissal.
A field of study, or the practice of enforcing rules; not punishment alone.
Revealing information that was hidden; public announcement.
Termination of employment; permanent removal from job.
A disagreement or argument, not necessarily a court case.
A department or business unit; the act of splitting into parts.
Reducing workforce or operations; not equipment downsizing.
A preliminary version of a document; not final or official.
Involvement or commitment; in HR, means employee motivation and participation.
Treating everyone identically; compare equity (fair treatment based on need).
Fair treatment based on individual circumstances; compare equality (identical treatment).
Increasing in severity or moving to a higher authority; raising an issue upward.
To make something easier or help it happen; not to force or direct.
Whether something is possible and practical to do; viability.
Money given for a purpose, not permission to do something.
A formal complaint about unfair treatment.
Repeated unwanted behaviour that causes distress, not a single incident.
Information or materials you contribute, not electrical input.
A deep understanding or realization, not just an observation.
Steps on how to do something, not a command.
Honesty and moral principles, not structural soundness.
Temporary or in-between, not lasting.
Student or trainee gaining work experience, not imprisoned.
First meeting or initial section, not a formal presentation speech.
A topic or problem under discussion, not a copy of a magazine.
Repeating a process to refine it, not a simple repeat.
A communication link between groups, not a romantic affair.
Official permission or document, not freedom to act.
Authority to act on behalf of others, not a command.
Profit per item, or edge of a page — context-dependent.
Deserve something based on quality or achievement.
A measurement standard, not necessarily using metres.
A significant point in progress, not literally a stone.
Wrongdoing or unethical behaviour, especially professional.
Important task or purpose, not a church building.
A self-contained unit of study or a component.
Driving force or buildup of energy; not physics momentum.
The confidence and spirits of a group, not a rule of behaviour.
A command or instruction, not a logical sequence.
Supervision and checks, not an accidental mistake.
The highest point or maximum level, not a mountain summit.
Someone of equal status or rank, not just a friend.
A range of investments or projects held together, not a briefcase.
A possible future outcome or opportunity, not a view or scenery.
Speed, or a fixed amount per unit (price, percentage), not a rank.
Written or stored data, not an achievement or to set down information.
Dependence on someone or something, not a connection or bond.
A place where things are stored or kept, not a report of findings.
A formal rebuke or scolding for wrongdoing.
A booking for accommodation or a table; can also mean a doubt or qualification.
A firm decision or determination; can also mean solving a problem or image clarity.
A pause or break from something difficult; temporary relief.
The ability to react quickly to changes or demands.
A document listing work experience and skills for job applications.
Selling goods directly to consumers, not wholesale.
Keeping or holding something; the ability to keep employees or remember information.
Taking back or withdrawing a statement or claim made earlier.
Withdrawing from a position or situation; can also be a quiet place for rest.
Looking back at past events; a display of past work.
A complete change in direction or decision; opposite of what came before.
An examination or assessment; can be a critical evaluation of a book, film, etc.
Reworking or changing something; studying material again before an exam.
A return to life, use, or popularity after a decline.
The art of persuasive speaking or writing; often implies exaggeration.
Strictness and precision; extreme severity.
A physical barrier or obstacle preventing progress; literal or figurative.
A plan showing how to reach a goal step-by-step; not a literal map.
The quality of being strong and able to handle stress or variation.
A person new to a job or activity; an inexperienced beginner.
A list of people assigned to a job or team, usually with their duties.
A raised platform for public speaking.
One turn or cycle in a series; a stage in a competition.
A summary of recent events or information; a gathering of animals.
A line of objects or people; not an argument or quarrel.
Lines of objects or people; not arguments or quarrels.
A set of criteria used to grade or evaluate work.
Sets of criteria used to grade or evaluate work.
A record of money at a bank; can also mean a description or explanation.
Active support or promotion of a cause, not the legal profession.
To support or promote; or a person who does so. Not necessarily a lawyer.
A fixed sum of money given regularly; not permission to do something.
Distribution or assignment of a resource or amount.
Heavy object that holds a vessel in place; also a person who hosts a broadcast.
An agreement or plan; also a musical adaptation.
Reduction in workforce due to natural departures, not deliberate cuts.
Data transmission capacity; also used for available time or mental space.
Legally enforceable; not just holding pages together.
A governing group; not a wooden plank.
Standard text used repeatedly, often in contracts or disclaimers.
A debt investment or certificate; not a personal connection.
To accumulate over time (often interest or benefits), not to occur suddenly.
To expect or plan for; not the same as delay.
Money owed that is overdue; not a location or body part.
To express clearly and coherently in speech or writing.
Something taken as true without proof; a belief or supposition.
A guarantee or promise of quality; not confidence in oneself.
People who watch or listen to a performance or broadcast; also a formal hearing.
To settle a dispute as a neutral third party, not to decide a sports match.
Following or obeying rules/requirements, not emotional attachment.
Postponing a meeting to a later date, not cancelling it.
An organization providing a service, not personal ability to act.
A convenient facility or service that adds comfort, not the main purpose of a place.
Someone who settles disputes between parties, not a sports referee.
